'''Ilham Al-Qaradawi''' (born 19 September 1959) is a Qatari professor of [[positron]] and [[radiation]] [[physics]] at [[Qatar University]] and adjunct professor of physics at [[Texas A&M University at Qatar]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title=Profile {{!}} Ilham Al-Qaradawi|url=http://ilhamalqaradawi.com/profile/|access-date=2020-10-21|language=en-US|archive-date=2022-09-27|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220927095617/http://ilhamalqaradawi.com/profile/|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>Al-Qaradawi, I. Y. Curriculum Vitae. [http://www.qu.edu.qa/static_file/qu/colleges/cas/faculty%20and%20staff/Math-Stat-Physics/documents/lham_CV_Formal_-_2013.pdf <nowiki>[PDF File]</nowiki>] ''Qatar University'' (2016). Retrieved from [https://www.qu.edu.qa/ http://www.qu.edu.qa/]</ref> She is the daughter of the Egyptian Muslim scholar, [[Yusuf al-Qaradawi|Yusuf Al-Qaradawi]].<ref>{{Cite web|date=2017-07-03|title=Arrest of Qardawi's daughter, son-in-law in Egypt: The list of charges they face|url=https://english.alarabiya.net/en/features/2017/07/03/Qardawi-s-daughter-son-in-law-detained-in-Egypt-The-list-of-charges-they-face|access-date=2020-10-21|website=Al Arabiya English|language=en}}</ref>

She is known for her work in positron physics, establishing the first slow positron beam facilities in the [[Middle East]] region.<ref name=":2">{{Cite web|title=Laboratories {{!}} Qatar University|url=https://www.qu.edu.qa/artssciences/laboratories|access-date=2020-10-21|website=www.qu.edu.qa}}</ref>  She has appeared on [[Al Jazeera Media Network|Al-Jazeera]] news network to address several nuclear energy problems in the world.<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite news|date=March 13, 2011|title=Professor comments on Japan's nuclear crisis|work=[[Al Jazeera Media Network|Al-Jazeera]]|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=09dU6lY4cqs&app=desktop|access-date=October 20, 2020}}</ref>

== Education and early career ==
Al-Qaradawi received her [[Bachelor of Science]] degree in [[physics]] in 1981 from [[Qatar University]] in [[Doha|Doha, Qatar]]. She then attended [[Bedford College, London|Bedford College]], [[University of London]] for her [[Master of Science]] degree in [[nuclear physics]] in 1984.<ref name=":0" /> She obtained her [[Doctor of Philosophy|PhD]] in [[positron]] [[physics]] from the [[Royal Holloway College]], [[University of London]] in 1991.<ref name=":0" /> She then worked as an assistant professor at [[Qatar University]] until 2009, when she was promoted to professor. She held a research fellowship at the [[University of London]] working on positron physics from 1998 to 1999.

== Research ==
Al-Qaradawi's research centers on [[positron]] and [[radiation]] [[physics]] and its applications. She led the efforts in establishing the first slow positron beam facility in the Middle East region, known as the "Qatar Positron Beam".<ref>{{Cite web|title=Positron Research {{!}} Ilham Al-Qaradawi|url=http://ilhamalqaradawi.com/research-interests/positron-research/|access-date=2020-10-21|language=en-US}}</ref><ref name=":2" /> The positron beam facility incorporates a Na-22 source and Tungsten mesh moderator, and is a magnetically guided beam with energies of 0-30 keV.  has established an environmental radiation measurement laboratory in [[Qatar University]] due to her interests in nuclear and radiation physics.

In 2016, she founded the first scientific societies in [[Qatar]], the [[Qatar Physics Society]]. She is currently the president, and holds training workshops for physics teachers and other activities in an effort to spread physics knowledge and improve physics education in the region.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|title=International News|url=http://www.aps.org/publications/apsnews/201804/international.cfm|access-date=2020-10-21|website=www.aps.org|language=en}}</ref>

== Awards and honors ==

* Recipient of the GR8! Women Magazine Award in 2013.<ref>{{Cite web|title=GR8! TV Magazine - The 3rd Petrochem GR8! Women Awards Middle East held amidst glitter & glamour|url=http://www.gr8mag.com/posts.php?id=711|access-date=2020-10-21|website=www.gr8mag.com}}</ref>
* Named top 500 most influential Arabs by [[Arabian Business]] magazine in 2012 and 2013.
* Named top 50 most influential Arabian women by [[Arabian Business]] magazine in 2012.<ref>{{Cite news|title=Most powerful Arab women: in pictures|language=en|work=ArabianBusiness.com|url=https://www.arabianbusiness.com/photos/most-powerful-arab-women-in-pictures-461357.html|access-date=2020-10-21}}</ref>
* [[Fellow of the Institute of Physics]] (IoP) in the UK.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1" />
* Qatar University Award for excellence in research, 2009.
